approach: Add one reading-gate check, `check_speed_timeline(reading, request)`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and wire it as one `step!(check_speed_timeline(reading, request));` line in `refusing_check`, right after `check_outcome_state`. That position keeps the existing test that expects `check_outcome_state` directly after `check_governance_coverage`. The check skips a reading with no capability or with a question. Otherwise it finds a speed request from the request text with `request_words` (reading.rs:3503): a whole-word cue (faster, quicker, slow/slower/slowest/slowly/slowdown, delay/delays/delayed, latency, timing/timings, speedup), `speed|speeds|sped|speeding` followed by `up`, `head start`, or a cut-verb (cut, save, shave, trim, reduce, shorten and their forms) within five words before a duration figure (digits plus s, ms, sec, second(s), min, mins, minute(s), glued or spaced). For such a request the reading needs an assumption whose trimmed text starts `Timeline:` (any case, as `code_surveys` does) that (a) names a crates/ path (`names_crates_path`, reading.rs:3838), and (b) either says no recorded timing exists ("no recorded timing", "no timing is recorded", "no timing recorded") or gives at least two duration figures and says where the delay sits (a whole word from delay, sits, slowest, longest, bottleneck). The error starts "the reading was refused because", is one line, and names what is missing and what to write. The check reads only the reading and the request, never the repository, so it is deterministic. Four more edits follow. (1) A seventh `READING_RULES` line in briefs.rs (at most 218 characters, because the existing test caps a line at 220 with its `- ` prefix) names `check_speed_timeline` and states what a `Timeline:` assumption holds. (2) New corpus cases in refusal_corpus.rs, new input-form tags, and a doc-comment/changelog/decision-log test. (3) A line in the fake reader (athena-agent/src/fake.rs) so nested runs and the existing drain test that asks "Speed up planning..." still pass the gate. (4) D163 in docs/decisions.md and a CHANGELOG.md entry. The root cause named in all of them: the reading stage checked a request's own figures only if the reader chose to, so readings were planned around stated timings with no stage timeline from the code. The fix is at the reading gate, where every speed request passes, so it covers the class and not one job.

decisions.choice: Enforce at the reading gate: one `step!` in `refusing_check` (reading.rs:3226-3252).
decisions.reason: Every reading passes this function; the corpus mechanism (`every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case`, refusal_corpus.rs:1061) forces a refusing case for it; it needs no model call. A refused reading is re-read once with the refusal text (reading.rs:473), so the reader learns what to write. The failure started when the reading was accepted without the timeline, so the fix goes there.

rejected.option: Prompt-only guidance (a line in reader.md or the briefs)
rejected.why: Prose only; the reader can ignore it, and that is the failure. The user default 'mechanism' says rules that matter are enforced by a check. The reader budget is 1997 of 2000 (docs/system-facts.md), and the prompt file is outside this job.

By the planner the reading is already accepted by the user and the criteria are fixed around the request's figure. The planner brief and prompts are out of scope. The planner sees no recorded timings either.
It runs after the producer has built the wrong thing; the failure is in planning.

decisions.choice: Check the shape of the timeline (label, crates/ path, at least two duration figures, where the delay sits, or an explicit 'no recorded timing'), not the truth of the figures.
decisions.reason: The gate reads only text and has no run data. The shape makes the reader read the code and write the stage order and where the delay sits before the criteria are fixed. 'No recorded timing exists' is an honest escape for a request with nothing measured, so the check does not force invented numbers.

rejected.option: Have Athena run the stages and measure them at reading time
rejected.why: Needs a build and test run per reading, unbounded cost and time, and is beyond one producer run.

rejected.option: Require a figure in the request before the check applies
rejected.why: The class includes 'make it faster' with no figure, and the failing job 20261025-190606-eebk also had a figure only in prose. Cues on words cover both.

decisions.choice: Detect a speed request with whole-word cues over `request_words`, plus `speed up`, `head start` and cut-verb-near-duration-figure, applied to the whole request text.
decisions.reason: `request_words` (reading.rs:3503) already splits bullets, numbered parts and hyphens, and lowercases, so cues are found in `-`, `*`, `1.`, `2)` and `(a)` parts and in a root-cause request that quotes introspections. Whole words keep 'slowloris', 'speedometer', 'quickstart' and 'timeline' from matching. A bare duration figure (`wait 30 seconds`) is not a cue.

rejected.option: Substring match like the fake reader's SPEED_WORDS
rejected.why: Matches inside other words and drifts from the gate.

rejected.option: Any duration figure in the request is a cue
rejected.why: Refuses retry-after and timeout settings that are not speed requests.

decisions.reason: The existing test `check_outcome_state_doc_names_root_cause_and_scope` (reading.rs:7725-7743) requires `check_outcome_state` right after `check_governance_coverage`. A step after it keeps that test as written. The check reads only reading and request, so it sits before the file-comparing checks.

rejected.option: Place it first or before check_code_survey
rejected.why: Changes which check names the refusal for existing corpus cases; no gain.

decisions.choice: Add a seventh `READING_RULES` line that carries what a `Timeline:` assumption must hold; do not extend `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE`.
decisions.reason: The reader-set budget (budgets.rs:34-39) is the prompt file, contract, defaults and catalog; the briefs.rs constants are not in it, so there is no token cost. The reading-rules section is 2151 bytes by my count (estimate, not measured) against the existing test cap of 2400 (briefs.rs:4430); a rule of at most 218 characters brings it to about 2370. The guide would add bytes with no room.

rejected.option: Raise the 2400 cap in the briefs test

decisions.choice: The fake reader (crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs:283) always adds one `Timeline:` assumption naming crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs and saying no recorded timing exists.
decisions.reason: The drain test `a_speed_improving_request_is_read_as_urgent_with_a_reason_and_an_ordinary_one_is_not` (drain.rs:7008) sends 'Speed up planning so it times out less.' through the real gate with the fake reader, whose reading has no Timeline; without this line that request would be refused twice and the test would fail. Always-on avoids a second cue list that can drift from the gate (athena-agent depends only on athena-data, so it cannot call the gate's detector). The text is a fixed string; no check logic is in the double. No test reads the old assumption text (searched).

rejected.option: Emit the Timeline only when SPEED_WORDS match
rejected.why: SPEED_WORDS and the gate's cues differ; a nested run whose request has 'delay' would be refused.

rejected.option: Edit the drain test to avoid the cue
rejected.why: Hides the dependency and weakens an existing test.

risks.risk: False refusals: a request that uses a cue word for something that is not a speed request (for example 'add a retry delay setting') is refused until the reader writes a Timeline.
risks.mitigation: The Timeline may say 'no recorded timing exists' and name a crates/ path, so the reader can clear it on its one re-read. Whole-word cues and the cut-verb-plus-figure rule keep 'slowloris', 'speedometer', 'timeline' and a bare 'wait 30 seconds' out; the lookalike corpus case pins that. The declared 5% is an estimate, not measured; the replay holds the job above 10%.

risks.risk: The check judges the shape of the timeline, not whether the figures are measured, so a reader can write invented numbers.
risks.mitigation: Stated in the doc comment and D163 as a limit. The check still forces the stage order, the crates/ path read and where the delay sits into the reading before criteria are fixed, which is what the three jobs lacked. Verifying the figures against run data is named as a follow-up.
